column1: # Targets allowed to run below the starvation floor, with why and where the
# evidence is. Format: target<TAB>reason<TAB>findings-ref<TAB>date-acknowledged
# This file is the difference between "we know" and "nobody looked". A target
# here still failed the floor -- it is simply failing for a reason someone
# wrote down and can be argued with. Entries older than 30 days are reported as
# stale by check-starvation.sh, because a cause that was true a month ago may
# have been fixed since.
# Remove an entry when the cause is fixed. If the gate then goes red, the cause
# was not what the entry claimed.
# A ROW HERE EXCUSES LOW THROUGHPUT. IT DOES NOT EXCUSE A TARGET THAT NEVER RAN.
# check-starvation.sh fails on "libFuzzer aborted during initial corpus
# execution" regardless of anything written here, and that is deliberate.
# WRITE THE CONSEQUENCE, NOT THE CAUSE
# A row here for spi_query_fuzzer used to read "dies on the upstream VACUUM context leak, one
# death per corpus replay". Every word of that is true and it hid the problem
# for months, because it describes the MECHANISM and leaves the reader to infer
# the cost -- and the obvious inference, "we lose one replay's worth of
# throughput", was wrong by three orders of magnitude. The target had never
# fuzzed at all. Say what the row costs, in numbers, or the next person will
# infer something comfortable too.
# THAT ROW WAS REMOVED 2026-08-25, and the sequel is worth recording.
# Its stated cause really was fixed: -detect_leaks=0 held, and the -und builds
# now exit 0. But the target was still producing zero new units -- for a
# completely different reason. Its seed corpus had grown to where REPLAY ALONE
# outlasts -max_total_time, so every job ends at the execution count it reached
# when replay finished and the mutation loop is never entered.
# The row had stopped describing anything true and was suppressing a live
# failure, which is precisely what this file warns against. It is also why
# check-starvation.sh's new INITED == DONE check is not suppressible: an
# acknowledgement can excuse a target that runs badly, never one that does not
# fuzz at all.
